 With AO3 offline, fanfic readers find ways to keep reading
 Tuesday, 3 November 2026, 00:41 
 Photo source: NBC News 
 After the Organization for Transformative Works announced a two-to-four-week shutdown following a security incident, readers have been sharing stories, tools and advice to help one another through the outage. 
 Archive of Our Own, also known as AO3, hosts more than 18 million works, including sexually explicit stories often called “smut” and fanfiction inspired by popular properties such as “Harry Potter,” “Twilight” and “Heated Rivalry.”
 This is reported by NBC News .
 Last week, the Organization for Transformative Works, the nonprofit behind AO3, said the site would be down for two to four weeks because of a “security incident.” The prospect of weeks without the platform’s uncensored stories and detailed tagging system prompted some readers to compare the outage to prehistoric times or describe it as a descent into madness.
 Advertisement 
 Readers have also rallied to help each other find stories. Moderators in Reddit’s r/AO3 community set up megathreads for sharing and locating copies of favorite works. Some AO3 writers are posting new chapters on Tumblr, while others are creating shared Google folders.
 Ashmita, a 23-year-old AO3 reader and fanfiction writer from India, built a web tool to help users connect Google Drive folders and navigate the hundreds or thousands of files they contain. “There are always debates, different opinions, and occasional fights within and between fandoms. But during the outage, I have seen people from completely different fandoms and backgrounds helping one another and working toward shared solutions,” she said. Ashmita asked to be identified by her first name only to protect her online privacy. “It has been a beautiful reminder of how much these communities care about each other,” she added.
 A public Google Drive link to a “Fanfic Emergency Fund,” created by author Berklie Novak-Stolz, has collected works from a wide range of fandoms and genres. “The horrors may persist, but so do we,” Novak-Stolz wrote in a letter to readers. “We’re all going to be okay thanks to the wonders of humanness and community and storytelling.” As of Sunday, the Organization for Transformative Works said it had no further updates on the outage.
 The organization urged users to follow safety practices while the site is down, including clicking links only from trusted sources, watching out for scammers and using unique passwords for each website. In a statement to NBC News, an Organization for Transformative Works spokesperson said the nonprofit would share updates on the “security incident” as soon as verified information became available.
 “AO3 and the OTW were founded by fans, for fans. That ethos remains at the heart of our mission today, and we love seeing how fans mobilize and support one another, both through and beyond AO3,” the spokesperson said. “As fan[s] ourselves, we deeply empathize with the frustration and despair of losing access to AO3 – and we’re heartened by the creativity, humor, and sense of community reflected in the flood of memes.”
 Other fanfiction sites and related platforms have used the outage to attract users. Wattpad wrote on X, “We’re here to support you during this difficult time.” Audio erotica platform Quinn also offered readers a discount code referring to AO3’s blackout.
 Advertisement 
 Some longtime readers said other sites cannot replace AO3, which they value for being funded entirely by its community and free of advertising. “To me, AO3 feels heartfelt,” Ashmina said. “It is a huge platform, but it still has the feeling of a niche community built by people who care deeply about what they are creating and sharing.”
